Mowbray Maternity Angels

By: Floris Kotze | Commission

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Tonight on Carte Blanche… no big budgets, no fuss — just heart, grit, and the miracle of life at Mowbray Maternity.

Unique Selling Point:
A rare good-news story in the public health sector — showing the remarkable women who keep South Africa’s future alive against all odds.



Summary:
Mowbray Maternity Hospital sits quietly between Groote Schuur and Red Cross Children’s Hospital. It doesn’t have the big budgets or shiny equipment. What it does have is heart. Nearly 10 000 babies are born here every year. Many arrive too soon. Many start life with a fight.

Led by the softly spoken but fiercely committed Ms Janine Joemat, this team of mostly female nurses and doctors keeps going no matter the odds. A 110-year-old building leaks and cracks. Budgets shrink. Yet inside these wards, hope is protected with everything they have.

They make plans. They brighten corridors. They comfort scared mothers. They care for babies as small as a packet of sugar. They even designed evacuation aprons so each nurse can carry four newborns to safety if disaster strikes.

This is a rare good-news story in the public health system. A small hospital with a giant spirit — where South Africa’s future is held gently in the palms of women who refuse to give up.

Further information:
Mowbray Maternity is one of the busiest maternity units in the province, but also one of the most overlooked. Nestled between two iconic institutions that attract donations and attention, Mowbray stands as a shining light built on determination rather than resources.

When a pipe burst recently flooded the neonatal ICU, it could have been disastrous. Instead, staff rushed in from home, rolled up their sleeves, and restored the unit within hours. Babies stayed safe. Not one was transferred. Not one mother was turned away. That resilience is stitched into every corner of this place.

But Mowbray is showing her age. The cramped wards and ageing infrastructure cannot meet the growing demand. Ms Joemat dreams of small improvements — a washing station or a kitchen where mothers can warm a bottle or make a cup of tea while they wait beside their premature babies. Tiny comforts that make a long and frightening journey a little easier.

Through Ms Joemat, we will meet three remarkable staff members who each carry a different part of this hospital’s heartbeat. Their stories — personal, real, and deeply South African — will reveal the true character of Mowbray Maternity: women working quietly, saving lives daily, and never expecting praise.

This is a story of courage behind closed doors. A story of care that doesn’t give up. A story that reminds us that even in a system under pressure, there are places — and people — worth celebrating.
